skill.name: copywriting
skill.description: Write rigorous, conversion-focused marketing copy for landing pages and emails. Enforces brief confirmation and strict no-fabrication rules.
skill.summary: Create clear, credible marketing copy from a confirmed audience and offer brief.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All four static alerts are false positives caused by ordinary copywriting guidance at the cited lines. The skill contains prose instructions and requests no system or network reconnaissance.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid buzzwords unless customers use them
Avoid stacking features without narrative flow.
- Avoid combining multiple messages into one element

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 126 advises avoiding buzzwords unless customers use them. It contains no instruction to inspect a system, device, process, or environment.
Line 168 advises arranging product features into a coherent narrative. It does not request system discovery or access.
Line 211 recommends isolating messages for clear copy and testing. It contains no system reconnaissance behavior.
Lines 32 and 33 compare clarity, outcomes, and features as writing priorities. They contain no network discovery instruction or operation.

content.value_statement: Unclear briefs often produce vague copy, weak calls to action, and unsupported claims. This skill confirms the strategy before creating structured, testable marketing copy.
actual_capabilities: Collects page goals, audience details, offer information, objections, proof, traffic sources, and awareness levels.
Summarizes the copy brief and assumptions for confirmation before drafting.
Creates sectioned page copy with headlines, subheadlines, calls to action, headers, and body text.
Provides two or three headline and call-to-action options with concise rationales.
Connects product features to customer benefits and outcomes.
Suggests isolated headline, message, and call-to-action tests.
limitations: Requires user confirmation of the copy brief before drafting final copy.
Does not invent statistics, testimonials, guarantees, or other supporting evidence.
Depends on accurate audience, offer, traffic, and proof information from the user.
Does not replace legal review, customer research, analytics, or live conversion testing.

use_cases.title: Launch a Product Landing Page
use_cases.description: Turn product, audience, and campaign details into structured landing page copy with clear calls to action.

use_cases.title: Clarify a Service Website
use_cases.description: Replace vague service language with specific benefits, outcomes, objection handling, and credible proof placeholders.

use_cases.title: Prepare Testable Campaign Copy
use_cases.description: Create focused headline and call-to-action variants for controlled marketing experiments.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Copy Brief
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare a copy brief for a [page type]. Ask for the audience, offer, primary action, objections, proof, traffic source, and awareness level.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before drafting when the available context is incomplete.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Landing Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create copy for [product] after I confirm the brief. Include a headline, subheadline, primary CTA, benefits, process, objections, and final CTA.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a complete page based on confirmed product and audience details.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Existing Copy
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this copy for clarity, specificity, customer relevance, unsupported claims, and CTA focus: [copy]. First summarize your recommended brief and assumptions for confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this to revise an existing page without changing its verified facts.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Copy Experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this confirmed brief, create three headline and CTA pairs for [audience]. Give each pair one distinct hypothesis and recommend a controlled test sequence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this to prepare focused variants for conversion testing.

output_examples.input: Write a landing page for invoicing software that helps freelance designers receive payment reminders automatically.
output_examples.output: Headline: Spend less time chasing invoices. Subheadline: Send professional invoices and schedule automatic reminders from one workspace. Primary CTA: Create your first invoice.

output_examples.input: Improve the CTA for a weekly operations newsletter aimed at startup founders.
Create a test plan for a project management landing page with an approved brief.
output_examples.output: Test the outcome-focused headline against the workflow-focused headline first. Keep the CTA and page structure unchanged, then test CTA wording after selecting a winner.

best_practices: Provide verified customer language, proof, objections, and offer details before requesting a draft.
Confirm the copy brief and correct assumptions before the skill writes final copy.
Test one major message or call-to-action change at a time.
anti_patterns: Do not request invented customer quotes, statistics, guarantees, or performance claims.
Do not combine several audiences, offers, or primary actions in one brief.
Do not approve polished language that hides an unclear value proposition.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the page type, primary action, audience, problem, offer, differentiator, desired outcome, available proof, traffic source, and awareness level.

faq.question: Why does the skill pause before writing?
faq.answer: It asks you to confirm the brief so the final copy reflects the correct audience, offer, goal, and assumptions.

faq.question: Can it write email copy?
faq.answer: Yes. The same brief process supports marketing emails when you provide the audience, purpose, offer, proof, and desired action.

faq.question: Will it create testimonials or statistics?
faq.answer: No. It can use verified evidence or mark clear placeholders when proof is unavailable.

faq.question: Does it provide copy alternatives?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides two or three headline and primary CTA options with a brief rationale for each.

faq.question: Can it guarantee higher conversion rates?
faq.answer: No. It creates clear, testable copy, but performance depends on the offer, audience, design, traffic quality, and experiment results.
